title: Ramayana Is Heading to Comic-Con — and Ranbir Kapoor Just Became India's Biggest Global Bet
excerpt: India's ₹1,000-crore mythological epic is eyeing a full trailer debut at San Diego Comic-Con this July, a Hans Zimmer–AR Rahman live concert in October, and a Diwali release that could redefine what Indian cinema means to the world.
body:
Something immense is stirring in the machine behind **Ramayana**, and for once, it isn't just Bollywood hype. According to multiple industry reports, director **Nitesh Tiwari** and producer **Namit Malhotra** are in advanced talks to launch the film's full trailer at **San Diego Comic-Con** later this month — the same stage where Marvel drops its bombs and DC lays out its universe. If confirmed, this would be the biggest Indian film to ever command a global pop-culture platform of this scale, and a signal that the makers aren't treating Ramayana as just another blockbuster. They're positioning it as a global cinematic event.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=3-wSEehDBVk</youtube>

The move follows a quiet but significant development: a three-minute promotional asset was certified by the CBFC on June 23, suggesting something imminent is about to drop. An earlier teaser, released on Hanuman Jayanti in April, racked up **18 million YouTube views** in its first 24 hours and turned Ranbir's serene, bow-wielding avatar of Lord Ram into one of the most discussed images in Indian pop culture this year.

And then Ranbir Kapoor went and said the quiet part out loud.


![Hanuman Jayanti — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Sri_Bhaktha_Hanuman.jpg/1920px-Sri_Bhaktha_Hanuman.jpg)



> **"When I became Raha's father, my perspective changed — and that made me take this challenge." — Ranbir Kapoor

The cast reads like a who's who of Indian cinema's current power structure."**



In an interview with Hollywood press following an LA screening, the actor confirmed he's playing a **dual role — Lord Ram and Lord Parashurama**. He also revealed that both parts of the film, released a year apart, will run a combined **six-plus hours**. Part 2 is already 50 percent filmed. This is not a movie. It's a saga being built in real time.

> "Playing Lord Rama is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. When I became Raha's father, my perspective changed — and that made me take this challenge." — Ranbir Kapoor

The cast reads like a who's who of Indian cinema's current power structure. **Sai Pallavi** as Sita brings the kind of luminous, earthy presence the role demands — her casting has been almost universally praised. **Yash**, fresh off the KGF mythology, steps into Ravana with the exact larger-than-life menace the role requires. **Sunny Deol** as Hanuman is inspired casting — the man is practically already a demi-god in the Hindi belt. **Ravie Dubey** plays Laxman, while **Arun Govil** — the original TV Ram from the 1987 *Ramayan* — portrays King Dasharatha in a beautiful generational handoff. The supporting cast reportedly includes **Rakul Preet Singh**, **Lara Dutta**, **Kajal Aggarwal**, and **Vivek Oberoi**, with persistent rumours of **Amitabh Bachchan** in an undisclosed role.

Behind the camera, the pedigree is staggering. Tiwari, who gave us **Dangal** (₹2,000 crore worldwide) and **Chhichhore**, is working with Oscar-winning VFX house **DNEG** — the studio behind *Oppenheimer*, *Inception*, and *Tenet*. Hollywood stunt director **Guy Norris** is choreographing the action. And the score is a historic dual composition by **AR Rahman** and **Hans Zimmer** — two Academy Award winners sharing a single soundtrack for the first time. The producers are planning a **live concert event in October** where both composers will perform together, an unmistakable move from the Best Picture playbook.


![Lord Ram — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/45/Lord_Rama_with_arrows.jpg)


The LA focus-group screening, held for a diverse international audience, reportedly drew a strong positive response — strong enough that the team accelerated their Comic-Con pitch. A source told Mid-Day: *"Comic-Con gives it a global platform. The idea is to present the mythological drama not just as an Indian epic, but as a cinematic spectacle to the world."* There's also talk of major **film festival screenings** before the theatrical release, which would put Ramayana alongside prestige fare on the international circuit.

## What the Diaspora Needs to Know

For NRIs in the US, this is personal. San Diego Comic-Con runs **July 22–26** — and if the Ramayana team takes that stage, it will be the first time an Indian film has commanded a presentation of this magnitude at SDCC. If you're in Southern California, you could be among the first people on the planet to see the full trailer on a massive screen. That's not just marketing. That's a moment.

**Ramayana Part 1** is slated for **Diwali 2026** (November), with Part 2 following **Diwali 2027**. With a reported budget exceeding **₹1,000 crore** and DNEG's world-class visual effects, this is Indian cinema's most audacious swing since *Baahubali*. The Diwali release window virtually guarantees wide international distribution — expect IMAX screenings across North America, the UK, and the Middle East.

Ranbir Kapoor almost turned down the role. He's spoken publicly about how playing Lord Ram felt too enormous a responsibility — this is a man who built a career on the complicated, the flawed, the morally ambiguous. It was fatherhood that changed his mind. If he pulls it off, this won't just be the role of his career. It could be the role of a generation.
